contexts.text: (A Spirit who was seen to make preparations to bury a dead body.) SE 1260.
He was unclean who had touched the dead, the slain, a man's bone, a grave (), all of which = things proper to man, which are dead and profane.
This represented the Lord's burial...
Thou shalt be buried in a good old age () = the enjoyment of all goods by those who are the Lord's; for they who die and are buried do not die, but pass from a dim life into a clear one. Explained.
They represented the Lord rising from the sepulchre... In the idea of a sepulchre there is something of burial, which they thus removed. HH 335. CL 412. SE 233.
The burial (of Sarah) = resuscitation.

Give me a possession of a burying-place with you () = that they can be regenerated. In the inward sense of the Word, a grave = life or Heaven, and in the opposite sense, death or Hell; for the Angels have no idea of a grave, because they have none of death; wherefore instead of a grave they perceive the continuation of life, thus resurrection; for man rises again as to the spirit, and is buried as to the body. And as burial = resurrection, it also = regeneration, for regeneration is the first resurrection of man, inasmuch as he then dies as to the former man, and rises again as to the new... AC 2916:3, Illustrated. AC 2938. AC 6459. AE 659.

The reason a grave, in the opposite sense, = death or Hell, is that the evil do not rise again to life: when therefore the evil are treated of, and a grave is mentioned, the idea of Hell comes to the Angels, which also is the reason that, in the Word, Hell too is called a grave. AC 2916:end, Illustrated.
As burial signified resurrection in general and in each person, the ancients were extremely solicitous about their burials, and about the places where they were buried. Illustrated.
That burial signified resurrection to life is evident also from other representatives, as that the wicked were not mourned for, nor buried, but were cast forth. Illustrated.
That I may bury my dead from before me () = that thus He may come forth and rise again from the night which prevails with them. To bury = to rise again. AC 2923. AC 2925. AC 2931. AC 2961.
In the choice of our sepulchres () = what is well-pleasing as to regeneration... Sepulchre = resurrection and regeneration.
None of us shall withhold from thee his sepulchre () = that all were ready to receive regeneration.
As burial = regeneration, it = those with whom the truth and good of faith can be received.
Bury thy dead () = that they should come forth from night and be resuscitated. To be buried = to rise again, or what is the same, to be resuscitated.

That I may bury my dead () = that they should come forth from night and be vivified. To be buried, here = to be vivified, because they are in the process of receiving faith... The reason I will bury my dead = coming forth from spiritual night and vivification, is also that when a former Church is dead a new one is raised up by the Lord in its place, thus there is life instead of death, and morning instead of night; and also because with everyone who is being reformed and made spiritual, what is dead of him is as it were buried, and what is new, that is, what is alive, rises again; thus instead of night with him, or instead of darkness and cold, there arises the morn with its light and heat. Hence it is that with the Angels, who are in the Lord's life, instead of the idea which a man has concerning the burial of the dead, there is the idea of resurrection and of a new life.
Abraham buried Sarah his wife () = that they received from the Lord truth conjoined with good. To bury = to regenerate.
To Abraham for a possession of a burying-place () = that it was from the Lord alone through regeneration. A sepulchre = regeneration.
Burial, therefore, = resurrection, because it is a full putting off.

Isaac and Ishmael his sons buried him () = that the representation of the Lord was now taken up by Isaac and Ishmael. To be buried = to be resuscitated and to rise again... Here to bury = the resuscitation of this state... for the representatives in the Word are continuous... and deaths do not signify any interruption, but continuation; therefore their burials = the representative resuscitated and continued in another.

As bones = falsities, and sepulchres, the evils in which they are, and as hypocrisy is an evil which outwardly appears good, but within is filthy from false and profane things, the Lord says... Ye are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outside, but within are full of the bones of the dead, and of all uncleanness ().
(Saw their own burial through my eyes.)
(Deborah) was buried beneath Bethel under an oak () = rejected in perpetuity. To be buried = to be rejected, for that which is buried is rejected.
Hence it was customary to weep for the dead when they were buried, although they knew that the corpse only was rejected by burial.

Rachel died, and was buried in the way of Ephrath () = the end of the former affection of interior truth... To be buried = the rejection of a former state, and the resuscitation of a new one. References. AC 4594. AC 6246.
And Jacob set up a statue on her grave () = that the Holy of spiritual truth will rise again there... Grave = resurrection.

Esau and Jacob his sons buried him () = that He rose again in the good and good of truth of the Natural. To be buried = resurrection... The reason to be buried = to rise again, is that when the body is dead, the soul rises again. Hence when burial is mentioned in the Word, the Angels do not think of the body which is being rejected, but of the soul which rises again... AC 5551:2.
I spoke with two whom I had known, on the same day they were buried, and with one who saw his own coffin and bier through my eyes... (This was Polhem, DMin 4752).
This influx manifests itself by so many being solicitous about their burial...
I will go down to my son to the grave mourning () = that the Ancient Church would perish.
In sorrow to the grave () = without hope of resuscitation... Grave = resurrection and regeneration; thus resuscitation; namely, of the Church.

Ye shall bring down my grey hairs in evil to the grave () = that spiritual good is about to perish, and thus the internal of the Church... To go down in good into the grave = to rise again and to be regenerated; wherefore to go down in evil into the grave is the opposite, thus to perish.
Bury me not I pray, in Egypt () = regeneration not in scientifics. To be buried = resurrection and regeneration.
Bury me in their burying-place () = such regeneration. To be buried = regeneration...
These things are signified by (Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob) in one sepulchre; for a sepulchre = resurrection into life, and regeneration. AC 6452. AC 6460.
Burial = regeneration. References.

In my grave which I have digged for me in the Land of Canaan, there shalt thou bury me () = that the Church is to be resuscitated where it was before. Grave, and to be buried = resuscitation. Explained.
And now I will go up and bury my father () = the resuscitation of the Church there from the internal. To be buried = resuscitation. AC 6522. AC 6547. AC 6551:end. AC 6555.

All that went up with him to bury his father () = all things which conduce to regeneration. To be buried = regeneration and resurrection... The reason to bury = both regeneration and resurrection, and also the resuscitation and renewal of the Church, is that all these significations involve the same thing; for regeneration is resurrection... and the resuscitation of the Church is effected through regeneration...
Because there were no graves in Egypt () = damnation.
Under Body, see this reference.
These goods are like whited sepulchres...
Not to be buried () = no resurrection to life.
He left nothing of His Human in the sepulchre. AC 10125:4.
These are they who are meant by those who went forth out of their graves. AR 845:end. AR 884:end.
His being buried signified the rejection of the residue of the human from the mother. TCR 130:end. ( = the glorification of His Human. AE 659:19.)
Not to be put in monuments, or not to be buried () = to remain in earthly and unclean things; and further, to be rejected as what is damned. Illustrated. AE 659.
What is such a faith but the sepulchre of our Lord... again closed by the soldiers of Pilate?
To bury (Gog) and cleanse the land () = to destroy them all, and thoroughly purge the Church of them.
Not to be buried () = to be damned. AE 650:62. AE 652:33.
The love of falsity is signified by a sepulchre on high ().
That graves = unclean things, thus also infernal things, from the corpses and bones in them, Illustrated.
Under Assyria, see this reference.
Such Genii and Spirits dwell in graves, etc.

Shall Thy mercy be told in the grave, and Thy Truth in destruction? () = that the Divine good and Divine truth cannot be preached in Hell, where and whence are evils and falsities... The grave = the Hell where and whence are evils; and destruction, the Hell where and whence are falsities. That the grave = Hell, is also evident from the fact that those who are in Hell are spiritually dead. Illustrated.

When those who are in falsities from evil are treated of, their grave means the Hell from which and in which is that falsity; but when those who are in truths from good are treated of, grave means the removal and rejection of falsity from evil, and burial, resuscitation and resurrection into life, also regeneration. Explained, Illustrated. AE 19.
Hence not to be buried = no resurrection to Heaven, nor regeneration; but resurrection to Hell, thus damnation. Illustrated.
The sepulchre where the Lord was, eminently = resurrection and regeneration.
That the Lord put off everything maternal in the sepulchre... For everything of that nature was dissipated in the sepulchre. Ath 161.
